from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Intermediate Value Theorem: Continuous functions crossing zero change sign.",
            "Imagine a hiker crossing a mountain range.",
            "If the hiker crosses, they must hit zero altitude."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT)", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        # Setup Axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-1, 5, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        ).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.add(axes)
        
        # Draw function
        func = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * (x - 2), color="#FFD700")
        self.play(Create(func), run_time=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#32CD32")
        
        a, b = 1, 3
        dot_a = Dot(axes.c2p(a, func.underlying_function(a)), color="#00FFFF")
        dot_b = Dot(axes.c2p(b, func.underlying_function(b)), color="#00FFFF")
        
        label_a = MathTex("a").next_to(dot_a, DOWN, buff=0.1).scale(0.7)
        label_b = MathTex("b").next_to(dot_b, DOWN, buff=0.1).scale(0.7)
        
        f_a = MathTex("f(a) < 0", color="#FF4500").scale(0.6).next_to(dot_a, UP, buff=0.1)
        f_b = MathTex("f(b) > 0", color="#FF4500").scale(0.6).next_to(dot_b, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(dot_a), Create(dot_b), Write(label_a), Write(label_b))
        self.play(Write(f_a), Write(f_b))
        
        c = 2
        root = Dot(axes.c2p(c, 0), color="#32CD32")
        label_c = MathTex("c", color="#32CD32").next_to(root, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(root), Write(label_c))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Topological Mapping: Configuration Space", [
            "We map curve point pairs to 3D space.", 
            "A surface represents all possible chords.", 
            "Midpoint and distance conditions reveal the square."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        param_space = Rectangle(width=3, height=3, color="#9370DB")
        curve_points = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#FFA500") for _ in range(5)]).arrange(RIGHT)
        func_f = MathTex("F(s, t) = 0", color="#20B2AA")
        boundary = DashedVMobject(Rectangle(width=3.5, height=3.5, color="#FFD700"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a parameter space (s, theta) for the square. Color #9370DB.
        self.place_in_area(param_space, 'B2', 'D4')
        self.play(Create(param_space))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#9370DB")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Map the square vertices to the curve points. Color #FFA500.
        # Define a continuous function F on this space. Color #20B2AA.
        # Visualize the boundary of the configuration space. Color #FFD700.
        self.place_in_area(curve_points, 'E2', 'E4')
        self.play(FadeIn(curve_points))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFA500")
        
        self.place_at_grid(func_f, 'A2')
        self.play(Write(func_f))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#20B2AA")
        
        self.place_in_area(boundary, 'B2', 'D4')
        self.play(Create(boundary))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")

        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Solution Strategy: Parity and Symmetry",

                           "We track square configurations along the loop.", 
                           "Constraints vanish, forcing the square into existence."])
        
        # Define elements

        square = Square(side_length=0.7, color="#00FFFF")

        self.place_at_grid(borsuk, "D4")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        group = VGroup(inscribed, square)
        self.place_in_area(group, "E2", "F5", scale_factor=1.2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Open Frontiers", [
            "The theorem holds for all smooth curves.", 
            "We explore rectangles and non-smooth loops.", 
            "The mystery of inscribed squares continues today."
        ])
        
        # Animation Elements
        curve = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([1.5 * np.cos(t) + 0.5 * np.sin(3 * t), 1.0 * np.sin(t), 0]),
            t_range=[0, 2 * PI]
        ).set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        square = Square(side_length=1.5).set_color("#32CD32")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#32CD32")
        self.place_in_area(curve, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        rect_label = Text("Rectangles", font_size=24, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(rect_label, 'B2')
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'E5', scale_factor=0.4)
        self.play(Create(square))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.wait(2)

outline.target_audience: Undergraduate mathematics students or math enthusiasts

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT)
sections.content: Briefly review the IVT: If a continuous function changes sign, it must cross zero. Visualize this as a hiker crossing a mountain range; if they start below a cloud layer and end above it, they must pass through the cloud.
sections.example: A hiker climbing from sea level to 1000m must pass through exactly 500m elevation.

sections.title: Problem Statement: The Inscribed Square
sections.content: Introduce the conjecture: Can every simple closed curve (a loop that doesn't intersect itself) have four points that form the vertices of a square? Show a circle and a random 'blob' shape side-by-side.
sections.example: Imagine a stretchy rubber band twisted into an irregular closed loop; we are searching for 4 points on that band that create a perfect square.

sections.title: Topological Mapping: The Configuration Space
sections.content: Explain how we map pairs of points $(x, y)$ on the curve to a 3D space. The set of all chords forms a surface. Explain that finding a square is equivalent to finding a point where the midpoint and distance conditions align.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'map' of all possible chords on the loop, where the axes represent the position of the two points on the boundary.

sections.title: The Solution Strategy: Parity and Symmetry
sections.content: Demonstrate the use of the 'winding number' or the antipodal map. If we rotate the square configuration, the difference between the 'midpoint' and the 'distance' constraints must vanish at some point due to continuous deformation.
sections.example: Using a robotic arm tracing the loop: as the arm adjusts to maintain a square, the continuous movement forces a intersection point where the 'square' property is satisfied.

sections.title: Summary and Open Frontiers
sections.content: Summarize that the theorem holds for all smooth curves (proven by Emch/Levien). Mention the generalization: the Inscribed Rectangle Problem (proven) vs. the Inscribed Square Problem for non-smooth curves (still an active area of research).
sections.example: Concluding with a digital animation of a square 'locking' into place on a dynamic, morphing organic shape.
